title: Polynomially Bounded Registers Yield Nondeterministic Logspace
statement: Let $L$ be a language of binary strings, and let a nondeterministic register program with $m$ registers and $d$ oracle languages have a finite control-state set with decidable equality. Suppose every oracle language belongs to $	ext{LOGSPACE}$. For some natural numbers $C_0,c_0$, assume that for every input $x$ there is a length $N$ such that every choice string of length $N$ makes the program halt, and each configuration before step $N$ along such a run satisfies the program's validity conditions and has every register value at most $C_0(|x|+1)^{c_0}$. Assume further that $x\in L$ exactly when some length-$N$ choice string makes the program answer yes. Then $L$ belongs to $	ext{NL}$, the class of languages decidable in nondeterministic logarithmic space.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a language of binary strings
The program has $m$ registers and $d$ oracle languages
The finite control-state set has decidable equality
Every oracle language is in LOGSPACE
For each input, some length $N$ makes every choice string of that length halt
Every pre-final run configuration satisfies the program's validity conditions
Every register value is at most $C_0(|x|+1)^{c_0}$
Membership in $L$ is equivalent to existence of a length-$N$ accepting choice string
